summary: Jinja2 3.x removes a number of long-deprecated APIs and folds some old extensions into the core compiler. The highest-impact migration issues are import/decorator renames, MarkupSafe import moves, removal of the old async patching module, and a few behavioral/template-level changes around built-in extensions and stricter security checks in filters such as xmlattr.

rules.old:
from jinja2 import Markup
value = Markup(html)
rules.new:
from markupsafe import Markup
value = Markup(html)
rules.why: Markup is no longer exported by Jinja and must be imported from MarkupSafe.

rules.old:
from jinja2 import escape
safe = escape(value)
rules.new:
from markupsafe import escape
safe = escape(value)
rules.why: escape is no longer exported by Jinja and must be imported from MarkupSafe.
The old contextfilter decorator was removed in favor of the unified pass_context decorator.
The old contextfunction decorator was removed in favor of the unified pass_context decorator.
The old evalcontextfilter decorator was removed in favor of pass_eval_context.
The old evalcontextfunction decorator was removed in favor of pass_eval_context.
The old environmentfilter decorator was removed in favor of pass_environment.
The old environmentfunction decorator was removed in favor of pass_environment.

rules.old:
from jinja2.filters import unicode_urlencode
qs = unicode_urlencode(value)
rules.new:
from jinja2.utils import url_quote
qs = url_quote(value)
rules.why: unicode_urlencode was renamed to url_quote and the old name was removed.
Legacy Context subclass resolution by overriding resolve is no longer supported; override resolve_or_missing instead.
The autoescape extension became built-in and the old extension entry point was removed.
The with extension became built-in and the old extension entry point was removed.
Async support no longer uses the old patching module; enable it explicitly on the Environment instead.
These legacy extensions are built into Jinja and specifying their removed extension paths will fail.

rules.old: {{ attrs|xmlattr }}  {# where attrs may contain keys like 'data x', 'a/b', 'a>b', or 'a=b' #}
rules.why: xmlattr now rejects attribute keys containing spaces and, in later 3.1.x releases, also '/', '>', and '=' for security reasons.

rules.old: Environment(enable_async=True)  # plus old runtime patching expectations
rules.why: Jinja 3 removed the old asyncsupport patching APIs entirely, so code must rely on native async support only.

rules.new:
# Upgrade runtime to Python 3.7+
import jinja2
rules.why: Jinja 3.1 dropped support for Python 3.6, so projects pinned to that interpreter must upgrade Python first.
